test_title: PYST 3: SSC Stenographer - English (Held On:12 Oct, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

I do not like / your paying / for the food / every time.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option (2) i.e "your paying".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the possessive form **"your"** being used with a gerund **"paying." **

 

 
• **"Do not like" **indicates a present dislike of something habitual. **"Your paying" **(gerund) treats "paying" as **a single concept**, which doesn't fully capture the ongoing nature**(every time__) **of the action the speaker dislikes.
 
• ** "You paying"** (**present participle**) emphasises the continuous action **(__repeatedly paying__)** that the speaker dislikes. This aligns better with the overall message.
 
• Hence, "you paying" is the clearer and more grammatically suitable choice to convey the speaker's ongoing dislike of someone else paying for the food.

**Therefore, the correct sentence is *"I do not like you paying for the food every time".***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Option 1) "every time" **correctly specifies the frequency of the action.
 
• **Option 3) "for the food"** correctly indicates what the payment is for.
 
• **Option 4) "I do not like"** is a correct expression of personal preference or feeling.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__**

__
 
• **Example 1:** Disliking a Specific Act (Gerund)

 
 
• Sentence: "I found **your interrupting** the meeting very rude."
 
• Here, "your interrupting" functions as a gerund, a noun phrase describing a specific instance of someone interrupting.
 
• The speaker dislikes the act itself (the interruption) that happened during the meeting.
 
 
 
• **Example 2: **Disliking a Habitual Action (Present Participle)
 
 
• Sentence: "I don't like **you leaving** your dirty dishes in the sink **all the time**__."
 
• In this case, "you leaving" is a present participle modifying the noun "dishes." It emphasizes the ongoing or repeated action of leaving dirty dishes in the sink.
 
• The speaker dislikes this habit, not just one specific instance.
